title: Hangman Game
story: _ _ _ _ _ — five blanks. You guess 'E'. _ E _ _ _. Then 'A' — wrong! One life gone. Six wrong guesses and the stick figure is fully drawn — game over. Hangman has taught spelling and vocabulary for generations. Build it.
why: Hangman combines string iteration, Vec for tracking guesses, conditionals for game state, and loops for the game round — a complete interactive program.
analogy: A crossword puzzle where each revealed letter is a small victory. Every wrong guess draws one more part of the hangman — head, body, arms, legs. The tension builds with each empty blank. Your program is the hangman artist and the puzzle master, all in one.
try_it: Add a function to check if a letter was already guessed. Implement full round simulation: guess P (correct), Y (correct), X (wrong), track display changes and lives. Add ASCII art for each life lost. Add a word bank with categories.
tips: Track the display as a parallel string: underscores become letters on correct guesses
Use a Vec[Char] for guessed letters — fast to check if already tried
Win condition: no underscores left in display. Lose condition: lives = 0
common_mistakes: Not checking if letter was already guessed — players shouldn't lose lives for repeats
Forgetting to update display on every correct guess
Case sensitivity: 'A' and 'a' should be treated as the same guess
